rubrics.justification: The model explicitly stated no image was provided and declined to describe morphology, avoiding fabricated claims; therefore it made no inaccurate morphological assertions.

It integrated key factors well: young age, normal BMI, good oocyte maturity, unexplained infertility, normal sperm, endometrial thickness, and first cycle status, though AMH was unavailable and some links were somewhat generic.

Reasoning was logical and internally consistent, clearly separating assumptions about embryo quality from patient-based prognosis; minor issue is that probability estimates rely heavily on assumed good morphology.

Recommendations were broadly consistent with IVF practice, especially favoring SET in a young good-prognosis patient and not routinely recommending PGT-A initially; however, suggesting hysteroscopy/SIS or ERA/ReceptivaDx as routine considerations is somewhat more aggressive than guideline-based standard care.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, cryopreservation, and future evaluation, though some advice remains generic because morphology was unavailable.
